name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "Arg525 sits in the kinase-domain helix that lines the ATP pocket. Replacing its positive charge with a neutral glutamine removes a contact needed to bind ATP, which weakens nucleotide binding and reduces catalytic activity.", "mechanism_class": "ligand_binding", "supports": ["E2", "E4", "E7", "E9", "E11"], "would_refute": "Ligand-bound experimental structures (e.g. 5P9J, which observes residue 525 with an ATP-site ligand) show the Arg525 side chain more than about 6 \u00c5 from any ATP, ATP-analogue, or inhibitor atom. A model of R525Q bound to ATP that keeps the same pocket geometry and contacts as the wild type would also refute it.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "UniProt's annotation for this exact substitution (E2) says it disturbs ATP binding, and InterPro places 517-529 in the active site (E7). Both point directly at ligand contact, which is the most specific evidence on this residue. Still missing: any structure-level check that Arg525 contacts the ATP site (G2), and any measurement of R525Q activity or ATP affinity (G1, G3)."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "Arg525 is part of the helix within the kinase C-lobe/catalytic region whose buried salt bridges or hydrogen bonds hold the fold together. Losing that network destabilises the helix and the domain, so the protein folds less stably and is degraded or misfolds, which lowers the amount of active BTK.", "mechanism_class": "stability_folding", "supports": ["E4", "E5", "E9", "E11", "E13", "E14"], "would_refute": "Predicted stability changes (e.g. FoldX or Rosetta ddG on the experimental structures, or on AF-Q06187-F1) show R525Q within about 1 kcal/mol of wild type, with no loss of helix contacts and no change in local backbone dynamics. Simulations of R525Q matching wild-type fluctuation would also refute it, as E10 already reports only local changes for other mutations.", "starting_rank": 2, "rank_rationale": "Strong conservation (E11: 0.967) and high predicted pathogenicity (E9, E13, E14) suggest the residue matters for the fold. But these scores do not say how, none of the retrieved studies tests R525Q directly (G1), and E10 reports only local dynamic changes for other clinical BTK variants, which weakens a global fold-loss story."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "Arg525 is one of the contact points at the SH2-kinase interface that holds BTK in an autoinhibited or activation-competent arrangement. The Gln substitution breaks this interdomain contact, which changes the conformational switch needed for activation by phosphorylation.", "mechanism_class": "domain_interface", "supports": ["E8", "E6", "E12"], "would_refute": "Full-length or SH2-kinase structures or models show that Arg525 has no atom within about 4 \u00c5 of the SH2 domain, or that its side chain points into the kinase core away from any interdomain surface. Alternatively, R525Q keeps the SH2-kinase interdomain contact network and the activation-loop conformation of wild type in simulation.", "starting_rank": 3, "rank_rationale": "The SH2-kinase mechanism (E8) is documented, but for other XLA substitutions in the SH2 domain, not for residue 525 in the kinase domain. No retrieved evidence places Arg525 at that interface (G2), so this is the weakest of the three. It remains worth testing because it is the only one that would explain activation defects without changing the active site."}
